weekly_thesis: W37 made robot intelligence an evidence-commitment problem. Monday asked whether VLA success, maps, world models, VLM explanations, and efficient memories expose the cue that should change action before failure. Wednesday enlarged that into evidence freshness: policies, maps, occupancy, generated physics, driving scenes, and navigation beliefs had to show when their support goes stale. Thursday made the same contract sharper through verifier-aware post-training, uncertainty-aware geometry, relative driving risk, evidence-order VLM calibration, and irreversible token admission. Friday then converted the week into transition accountability: a memory, generated future, 3DGS map, safety layer, cache, or dexterous contact structure is useful only if it states which transition it may authorize and which deployment condition revokes that authority.

clusters.cluster: VLA authority shifts from final success to transition-level evidence gates
clusters.why_it_matters: The week repeatedly rejects terminal success as the only VLA evidence. FailureSpot, RoboSPA, and What Matters When split timestamped failure, spatial-procedural difficulty, and conditional visual grounding; CR-VLA-Force and Where Success Breaks make force or boundary signals interrupt the policy; HaWMPO, HuRo, IMLE-VLA, FARM, and UniMPA ask whether imagined worlds, robotized human videos, faster action heads, predictive states, and memory banks are authorized to change a transition. APRL should evaluate the permission signal before the final success label.
clusters.confidence: High - every available listing day contributed independent VLA evidence around failure timing, grounding, force, boundary, world-model, pretraining, or memory authority.
clusters.lab_action: Run one manipulation suite with task difficulty, conditional visual grounding, force interruption, failure-boundary labels, world-model rollouts, robotized pretraining, single-step action heads, predictive-state readouts, and memory banks as separate interventions; compare action delta, warning lead time, jerk, unsafe permission, recovery, and OOD success.

paper_autopsies.title: FailureSpot: Label-Efficient Timestamp-Level Failure Detection for Vision-Language-Action Models
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: VLA failure detection is often evaluated at the trajectory level, after the policy has already taken wrong actions.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says trajectory-level labels turn normal pre-failure behavior into noisy failure supervision.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: Failure supervision should be aligned to the moment when the action stream becomes abnormal, not to the final episode label.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Use unlabeled action chunks to generate weak timestamp signals, then spend dense labels only on uncertain trajectories.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The method detects inconsistent consecutive chunks, frozen or idle actions, and aggressive random motions before fine-tuning with active timestamp labels.

decisive_evidence.claim: The paper targets fine-grained timestamp-level VLA failure detection.
It combines action-derived weak supervision with active learning for timestamp annotation.
APRL should ask how early a detector changes continuation, recovery, or stop decisions before terminal failure.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If action-derived weak labels mostly mark benign exploration or pause behavior, timestamp localization can become a style detector rather than a failure detector.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Evaluate false alarms on slow cautious policies and missed alarms on smooth but wrong object-selection failures.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Treat failure as a time-localized control variable, not a post-hoc episode attribute.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Direct for long-horizon VLA manipulation; less direct for short single-step actions where failure timing is ambiguous.

paper_autopsies.title: CR-VLA-Force: Learning Control-aware Compliance VLA Model for Robust Contact-rich Robotic Manipulation
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Force-aware VLA policies can still execute long action chunks before force feedback changes the command.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says force-aware VLA models remain weak at precise force tracking and rapid successive adjustment.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: Contact evidence should be allowed to interrupt or reshape an action chunk before unsafe force accumulates.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Encode force signal sequences with visual-language features and treat compliance as a control-aware VLA capability.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The proposed CC-VLA framework uses multimodal mixture-of-experts features so force and visual-language evidence can jointly shape reactive control.

decisive_evidence.claim: The paper targets action-chunk latency and force-tracking limits in contact-rich manipulation.
It introduces Control-aware Compliance VLA for reactive control with force/torque perception.
APRL should score whether force evidence changes the remaining command before a contact failure completes.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If gains disappear when contact timing, material compliance, or object geometry changes, the method may be fitting familiar force profiles.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Test delayed force spikes, near-identical visual states with different contact stiffness, and action chunks that must be interrupted mid-execution.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Treat contact as a permission signal over the next action, not as an auxiliary observation.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Direct for force/torque-equipped manipulation; weaker for tasks without contact sensing or chunked policy execution.

paper_autopsies.title: HaWMPO: Hallucination-Aware World Model-based Policy Optimization for Generalist Robot Policy
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: VLA post-training can use online robot reinforcement learning, but physical rollouts are costly, slow, and risky.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says world-model rollouts can hallucinate long-horizon state transitions and mislead policy learning.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: Imagined experience should not have equal authority unless its reliability is scored at the action-chunk level.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Attach hallucination scores to action-conditioned generated image sequences and soften policy optimization rewards accordingly.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: HaWMPO estimates generated-rollout reliability and uses a Reward-Soft mechanism to suppress unreliable action chunks during GRPO-style post-training.

decisive_evidence.claim: The paper targets world-model hallucinations in long-horizon VLA policy post-training.
It reports LIBERO gains and real-world G1 manipulation improvement from 67.5 percent to 80.0 percent across two tasks.
APRL should weight imagined robot rollouts by hallucination risk before using them as training evidence.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If hallucination scores fail under new objects, cameras, or contact regimes, the optimizer may still amplify plausible but wrong trajectories.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Compare imagined rollouts with physical rollouts under hidden object displacement, long-horizon dependency, and contact-state changes.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: A world model is a source of proposed evidence, not a free substitute for physical interaction.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Direct for VLA manipulation post-training; weaker for tasks whose world-model error is not visually observable.

paper_autopsies.title: View-Structured Conformal Prediction for 3D Gaussian Splatting
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: 3DGS uncertainty maps are often visually inspected without finite-sample guarantees for a whole rendered view.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says marginal pixel coverage can look acceptable while view-level coverage fails.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A rendered scene should expose view-wise uncertainty before a robot uses it for localization, collision, or inspection.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Treat novel-view synthesis as structured regression and require coverage over a fraction of pixels in a new view.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: VSCP separates renderer-provided spatial shape from a transferable view-difficulty multiplier, then calibrates across held-out views.

decisive_evidence.claim: Pixel-pooled calibration reaches 89.9 percent marginal pixel coverage but only 61.4 percent view-event coverage at a 90 percent target.
View-CP reaches 91.7 to 92.0 percent view-event coverage in the reported setting.
APRL should ask whether 3D maps report action-relevant uncertainty at the view or task level.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If calibrated view boxes do not predict downstream relocalization or collision-query risk, uncertainty remains visual rather than robotic.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Evaluate viewpoint sweeps where small uncovered regions contain the obstacle, target handle, or localization feature needed for action.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Uncertainty must be calibrated at the unit where decisions are made.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Direct for view synthesis and mapping; needs task-level translation before certifying robot actions.

paper_autopsies.title: HuRo: Robotizing Human Videos for Scalable VLA Pretraining
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Large human video corpora look attractive for robot policy learning, but embodiment mismatch can make visual imitation non-executable.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says existing approaches either robotize task-matched videos or separately align observation and action at scale.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: Human videos become useful robot supervision only if missing intermediate signals and robot-aligned actions are reconstructed well enough for execution.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Convert heterogeneous human videos into robot-aligned observations and action trajectories, then test whether scale helps VLA pretraining.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: HuRo infers missing intermediate signals across annotation levels and builds robotized episodes before downstream manipulation pretraining.

decisive_evidence.claim: The paper constructs about 630K robotized episodes and 142M processed frames from five human-video sources.
Increasing robotized pretraining scale improves real-world task completion from 51.5 percent to 80.3 percent and OOD completion from 34.9 percent to 72.2 percent.
APRL should judge human-video pretraining by execution transfer under spatial and visual shifts, not by clip count alone.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If gains disappear when action retargeting or visual robotization is stress-tested separately, scale is not the causal explanation.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Hold video scale fixed and ablate visual robotization, action retargeting, missing-signal inference, and OOD object placement.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Treat robotized video as executable supervision only after testing which alignment step changes the robot action.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for manipulation pretraining; weaker for tasks whose human motions lack robot-actuator or contact analogues.

paper_autopsies.title: RIDE: Relocalization-Informed Depth Estimation with 3D Gaussian Splatting
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Render-match-PnP relocalization is often treated as a pose-recovery tool, while dense depth is learned by a separate model.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says relocalization correspondences carry metric geometry that is usually overlooked for depth estimation.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A 3DGS map is robot-useful if sparse pose correspondences can correct dense perception through observation gaps.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Fuse PnP-RANSAC inlier depth from a metrically scaled 3DGS model with pretrained video-depth priors for robot RGB streams.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: RIDE combines sparse metric depth, global/local correction, and temporal memory to support dense depth through intermittent observations.

decisive_evidence.claim: The method estimates dense metric depth from a robot RGB stream using a metrically scaled 3DGS model.
It is evaluated on robot sequences without fine tuning and reports improved depth accuracy and temporal consistency over scale-only calibration.
APRL should evaluate 3DGS maps by depth and relocalization recovery under observation gaps.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If improvement vanishes when PnP inliers are sparse or dynamic objects dominate, the map is not robust enough for deployment.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Sweep occlusion length, map scale error, dynamic clutter, and view angle while measuring depth drift and pose recovery.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Use relocalization geometry as a correction signal, not just a success/failure pose output.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Direct for mapped robot environments; weaker for unstructured scenes without a maintained metric 3DGS model.

paper_autopsies.title: ReactHuman: A Physics-Grounded Benchmark for Human-Like Reactive Decision-Making in Embodied Multimodal LLMs
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Embodied MLLM evaluation often measures passive video understanding or deliberate long-horizon planning.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says no prior benchmark measures whether a model can turn physical understanding into immediate safety-critical action.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A household robot decision core must be judged by the physical consequences of committed reactions, not by plausible explanations.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Put the evaluated MLLM inside simulated humanoid hazard scenes and execute every committed plan.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: ReactHuman uses 17 event families, reproducible rigid-body scenes, adversarial object appearances, and a five-metric reaction suite.

decisive_evidence.claim: The benchmark contains over 1,000 bit-for-bit reproducible scenes with 240 Hz rigid-body simulation ground truth.
Seven evaluated MLLMs mishandle roughly one hazard in three, and the failures do not shrink with model scale in the reported study.
APRL should evaluate embodied reasoning by executed reaction safety under misleading appearance and motion cues.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If improved controllers solve reaction timing while the language model still chooses unsafe goals, the benchmark conflates policy and motor layers.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Hold the hazard physics fixed while swapping appearance, reaction deadline, embodiment reach, and available evasive actions.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Physical understanding earns authority only when the chosen action survives execution.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for household and humanoid safety; less direct for slow inspection tasks where reaction timing is not dominant.

paper_autopsies.title: Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Long-video systems often choose between dense visual tokens that are expensive and text summaries that lose fine visual attributes.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract states that language memories preserve temporal structure better, while pixels remain decisive for attribute-level perception.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: The system should retrieve frames only when the query actually needs visual evidence that text memory cannot carry.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Create a dual-track narrative index and route each query through a Visual-Need Router before bounded keyframe retrieval.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: An edge pass builds story and micro-log memory; cloud-side reasoning retrieves frames only for perceptual questions.

decisive_evidence.claim: The router triggers keyframe retrieval for perceptual questions and keeps temporal-structural questions in language space.
The framework caps per-query frame consumption regardless of video length while reporting strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.
APRL should treat robot video memory as query-conditioned evidence admission, not a fixed frame budget.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If decisive safety cues are rare and not predictable from the language memory, the router may skip exactly the frames needed for action.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Place task-critical visual changes in brief off-center frames and ask queries whose language story sounds sufficient but is wrong.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Retrieve pixels only when the decision contract names what text cannot know.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Useful for inspection robots and long-horizon video agents; needs safety guards before online control use.

new: The week adds explicit transition accountability: action heads, memories, maps, generated futures, and constraints must state which transition they authorize.
Sep 8 had no arXiv listing in cs.CV or cs.RO, making the week unusually compressed but not incomplete.
Radar, haze, street-language Gaussian fields, and mmWave splats turn degraded sensing into a geometry release gate rather than a side benchmark.
strengthening: Evidence admission strengthened across VLA failures, force interruption, verifier-aware post-training, predictive-state readouts, and hard constraints.
Robot-usable geometry strengthened through 3DGS navigation, LiDAR-wheel-radar odometry, learned occupancy, conformal 3DGS, degenerate registration, RIDE, and GRADE.
World-model evaluation strengthened around physical variables, ego-motion, topology, tactile correction, and feedback timing.
commoditizing: Generic world-model, VLA scaling, and token-pruning claims look weak unless they expose the specific evidence variable that changes action or recovery.
contradiction: The week rewards richer context but repeatedly warns that stale memories, unverified imagined futures, degraded sensors, and compressed caches can create false authority.
missing_axis: No public benchmark yet ties transition evidence, degraded-sensor geometry, physical world-model commitments, VLM evidence use, and embodied recovery into one closed-loop robot episode.

strategy_board.why_now: W37 repeatedly exposed the same gap across failure detection, force feedback, world-model rollouts, robotized pretraining, single-step action heads, and hard constraints.
strategy_board.what_others_optimize: Most papers still optimize success rate, throughput, or isolated benchmark accuracy.
strategy_board.our_contrarian_bet: APRL should own the transition-level evidence labels that decide when a policy may continue, interrupt, recover, or fall back.
strategy_board.required_moat: Robot episodes with transition labels, force events, stale memory, imagined rollout mismatch, predictive-state warning, and recovery outcomes.

score_rationale.strategic_fit: Directly matches APRL interests in robot perception, VLA, and failure analysis.
score_rationale.asymmetry: A small lab can win by owning hard failure episodes rather than model scale.
score_rationale.timing: The field is naming evidence gates before standards settle.
score_rationale.tractability: A tabletop probe with force, memory, and recovery labels is feasible in one week.
score_rationale.defensibility: Curated transition labels and recovery traces are difficult to copy.
score_rationale.scientific_depth: The benchmark separates evidence authority from final task success.

strategy_board.one_week_probe: Record five manipulation episodes where force, memory, visual grounding, or predictive-state warning should change the next action.
strategy_board.four_week_build: Compare VLA, single-step action head, memory bank, force-interruption, and safeguard variants on the same transition labels.
strategy_board.success_metric: Transition evidence predicts recovery, unsafe continuation, and action correction before terminal success diverges.
strategy_board.stop_condition: Stop if transition labels add no information beyond terminal success and ordinary confidence.
strategy_board.paper_path: Transition accountability for evidence-gated VLA control.
strategy_board.asset_path: Synchronized robot episodes, transition labels, force traces, predictive-state warnings, memory retrieval logs, and recovery outcomes.

strategy_board.why_now: This week tied 3DGS, LiDAR, radar, learned occupancy, conformal uncertainty, street language fields, and relocalization depth to deployment failures.
strategy_board.what_others_optimize: Reconstruction appearance, isolated pose error, segmentation accuracy, or rendering quality.
strategy_board.our_contrarian_bet: A map or reconstruction should enter the robot loop only if it survives the sensor condition that will break the task.
strategy_board.required_moat: Repeated robot routes with haze, occlusion, sparse views, radar/RGB disagreement, dynamic objects, and downstream action outcomes.

score_rationale.strategic_fit: This is core SLAM, mapping, and robot perception territory.
score_rationale.timing: Gaussian maps and foundation geometry models are converging now.
score_rationale.tractability: A corridor and tabletop degraded-sensor suite can start quickly.
score_rationale.defensibility: Sensor-survival labels and repeated robot routes become reusable assets.
score_rationale.scientific_depth: The work connects representation uncertainty to action consequence.

strategy_board.one_week_probe: Collect a small route/tabletop suite with haze, occlusion, sparse views, radar or depth disagreement, and moving clutter.
strategy_board.four_week_build: Evaluate 3DGS, LiDAR odometry, learned occupancy, conformal uncertainty, radar depth, and street semantic maps against downstream robot tasks.
strategy_board.success_metric: A degraded-sensor validity score predicts relocalization failure and task failure better than visual quality or ATE alone.
strategy_board.stop_condition: Stop if ordinary pose or reconstruction metrics fully explain downstream failures.
strategy_board.asset_path: Sensor-degraded routes, maps, uncertainty outputs, relocalization traces, semantic persistence labels, and downstream outcomes.

strategy_board.why_now: World-model papers this week asked whether generated futures preserve physics, tactile state, ego-motion, topology, and feedback timing.
strategy_board.what_others_optimize: Visual plausibility, rollout loss, or policy gain in separate setups.
strategy_board.our_contrarian_bet: A generated future should be blocked from policy authority unless it preserves the physical variable that changes the next action.
strategy_board.required_moat: Counterfactual futures with tactile/contact labels, camera motion, topology, physical-rule violations, and feedback schedules.

score_rationale.strategic_fit: Close to APRL robot execution, though world-model integration may be heavier.
score_rationale.asymmetry: A validity benchmark can expose failures in larger models.
score_rationale.timing: World-action model evaluation criteria are unsettled.
score_rationale.tractability: A replay probe is feasible; full policy integration is harder.
score_rationale.defensibility: Feedback schedules and physical-failure labels become reusable.
score_rationale.scientific_depth: The test separates physical commitment from visual fluency.

strategy_board.one_week_probe: Replay two manipulation and one navigation scene with generated futures that disagree on contact, topology, or ego-motion.
strategy_board.four_week_build: Compare world models, tactile predictors, topological planners, and hallucination-aware policy updates by action ranking and recovery outcomes.
strategy_board.success_metric: Physical-commitment metrics predict closed-loop action ranking better than ordinary video quality or rollout score.
strategy_board.stop_condition: Stop if all world-model metrics rank methods identically after realistic feedback is included.
strategy_board.paper_path: Physical commitment tests for robot world models.
strategy_board.asset_path: Rollout traces, physical-variable labels, feedback schedules, topology constraints, counterfactual actions, and policy outcomes.
